newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Long Belgian OLOs torn between data, tennis hero.
newsitem.headline: Long Belgian OLOs torn between data, tennis hero.

text.p: Dealers in the Belgian government bond (OLO) and futures market are counting on two interruptions to the prevailing calm on Friday:
- the French Open semifinal featuring Belgian tennis hero Filip Dewulf beginning at lunchtime
- and the 1230 GMT release of U.S. jobs data, which players hope will liven up trade and allow for a reversal of long positions built up recently.
"I would rather bet on the tennis than the market," a trader said. A slight rise in job creation in the U.S. in May was already discounted.
Play starts at 1100 GMT, with Dewulf facing Gustavo Kuerten of Brazil on Centre Court.
On a more secular note, U.S. payrolls growth is forecast at 219,000 in May, up from 142,000 in April, but economists say a large part of the increase is due to seasonal adjustments.

"In the U.S. the risk is to higher than expected job creation," ABN-AMRO said. "At last...today's non-farm payrolls should bring some action," Kredietbank added, forecasting bond-unfriendly data. "Do not expect yields to go far above six percent...in Belgium at this level cash-rich investors will get back into the market."

One trader said the market, practically steady in Friday morning trade, was looking for price gains as an excuse to take profits. "In the last few days we have only seen buyers... professionals...a lot of longs have been set up."
He said that once the 10-year OLO yield reached 5.85 percent positions would be sold. "Six percent then is not that far away." The 10-year benchmark yielded an unchanged 5.90 percent at 0930 GMT.
After the weekend the market might see EMU-inspired action. This would depend on any fresh statements from the new French government on its stance on Europe's single currency project.
Sunday's and Monday's meeting of European economics and finance ministers will be scrutinised.
"It could cast a shadow over the market...there are some serious euro-sceptics in the French government now...but it would cause only a temporary back-up in yields," the trader said.
His focus was on the tennis.
"He (Dewulf) is in with a chance...although he has played three matches more," he observed.
